# Notes: #5064 "Improve DXIL Validator Testing Infrastructure"

## Ground truth

Registered compiler: `main-debug` (`build\Debug\bin\dxc.exe`, relative to the repo root),
batch-019.

- `dxc --version` self-reports commit `7665270b9` ("Merge remote-tracking branch 'origin/main'
  into triage") — a fork-local merge commit, not the public upstream SHA.
- The batch's registered public ground truth is `89e2f98e29c289ae8ad9e00dd310104fea9fd7df`
  (`.cache/compilers/main-debug.json`'s `git_commit` field, consistent with this batch's other
  issues, e.g. `4958/verdict.json`).
- Per the skill's "verify by tree, not by SHA" rule, tree-equivalence was checked directly rather
  than trusting the self-reported SHA:
  - `git diff --name-only 7665270b9 89e2f98e29c289ae8ad9e00dd310104fea9fd7df` →
    **5315 files changed, 0 outside `.github/skills/dxc-issue-triage/`** (all of them prior
    batches' triage data additions). So the built tree and the cited public commit are identical
    everywhere that matters for this issue.
  - Negative control — the same diff against a genuinely older tag,
    `git diff --name-only v1.4.1907 89e2f98e29c289ae8ad9e00dd310104fea9fd7df` →
    **6992 files changed, all outside the skill dir**. This proves the diff/filter method can
    actually detect real differences, so the "0 outside the skill dir" result above is meaningful
    and not a vacuously-passing check.
  - The exact ground-truth SHA is a shallow single-commit ref in this checkout
    (`git rev-list --count` = 1), so the ancestor-relative control used elsewhere in this batch
    (`<sha>~N`) does not resolve against it directly; the tag-based control above was used
    instead and gives the same assurance.
- Both commands are captured verbatim, with full command lines and exit codes, in
  `manual-case-lit-validator-coverage.txt` (generated by `capture-lit-validator-coverage.py`,
  not hand-transcribed).

Conclusion: the registered Debug build is a valid ground-truth stand-in for
`89e2f98e29c289ae8ad9e00dd310104fea9fd7df` for the purposes of this issue.

## Why this issue has no shader repro

Issue #5064 is labelled `tech-debt` and asks the project to improve how the DXIL *validator
itself* is tested — extend `dxv`, replace the current TAEF/GoogleTest `%dxilver` workflow with
something LIT-compatible, and add coverage for external validator loading. There is no shader,
no single `dxc` invocation, and no compiler-output symptom to reproduce; the "bug", if any, is in
the test harness's wiring, not in compiled shader behaviour. Per the skill's guidance for
build-system/tech-debt issues, the investigation instead targeted "the producing instrument":
the lit test-discovery configuration and the git history of the relevant test/runner files.

## Timeline / cross-references

`gh api repos/microsoft/DirectXShaderCompiler/issues/5064/timeline` shows **zero
`cross_referenced` events** — no PR or commit anywhere in the repo's history links back to this
issue number. The only timeline events are `labeled`/`unlabeled` (`needs-triage` → `tech-debt`)
and one `milestoned` event (`Upstream Support`, 2023-06-30). So none of the resolution evidence
below was found "for free" via a linked PR; it had to be found by directly probing the current
state of the test tree.

## Finding 1: the DXIL-validator FileCheck tests are excluded from lit discovery (asks 1–3, still open)

`tools/clang/test/HLSLFileCheck/validation/` holds ~150 `%dxilver`/`%dxv` FileCheck-style
`.ll`/`.hlsl` test files — exactly the kind of test the issue describes wanting a LIT-compatible
workflow for (e.g. `wavesize/max-too-large.ll`, `infra/auto-dxilver.hlsl`).

`tools/clang/test/HLSLFileCheck/lit.local.cfg` (at ground truth) reads:

```
# HLSL Change - Hide files in CodeGenHLSL directory - they are tested by existing
# TAEF tests (CompilerTest, DxilContainerTest, LinkerTest)
config.suffixes = []
```

Setting `config.suffixes = []` makes lit discover zero test files anywhere under this directory,
regardless of what files exist there. (The comment text — "Hide files in CodeGenHLSL directory"
— is a copy-paste artifact; this file lives in `HLSLFileCheck`, not `CodeGenHLSL`. The sibling
`tools/clang/test/DXILValidation/lit.local.cfg` has the same pattern with a matching, if also
misleading, comment about "DxilValidation".)

This was set by commit `b503da7084b4200909d2a3b7dcfc18e8d2944eec` (PR #5537, "DXC Tests: Filter
out unsupported test, add verbose option and improve output", 2023-08-18), which replaced an even
blunter blanket disable, `config.unsupported = True`, introduced by `f5442b1fb577e79829807b4ec0b8eee0d6e45b48`
(PR #4822, "Disable lit shtest suites", 2022-11-29). PR #5537's own commit message states the
motivation plainly: "there was over 10K of unsupported tests found by LIT discovery" — this is a
blanket exclusion for build-configuration reasons (most of the ~10K were legitimately unsupported
under the SPIR-V-disabled default config), not a deliberate migration decision about the
validator tests specifically, but the practical effect for this issue's ask is the same: the
validator FileCheck tests are unreachable by `lit`/`check-all`.

**Directly measured** (not merely inferred from config; `lit --show-tests` only enumerates tests,
it does not build or execute `dxc`/`dxv`, so this is read-only and required no rebuild):

```
python utils\lit\lit.py --show-tests --param=build_mode=Release build\tools\clang\test\HLSLFileCheck
  -> "contained no tests"
python utils\lit\lit.py --show-tests --param=build_mode=Release build\tools\clang\test\DXILValidation
  -> "contained no tests"
```

Both confirmed empty at ground truth. Full output in `manual-case-lit-validator-coverage.txt`.

**The gap is still live, not merely historical.** New files continue to be added to this
lit-excluded tree well after the exclusion landed:
`git log -1 -- tools/clang/test/HLSLFileCheck/validation/wavesize/max-too-large.ll` →
`dcb618a2f1b7f4265fc2b77c12291f76eb334ae3` (2024-01-22, PR #6172, "Fix bad WaveSize non-range
PSV0 and improve things") — 5 months after PR #5537 excluded the directory from lit discovery.
Developers are still adding tests here despite them never running automatically.

**How these tests actually run today:** only through a manual, one-directory-at-a-time TAEF
invocation. `utils/hct/hcttest.cmd` has a `-filecheck <path>` mode
(`MANUAL_FILE_CHECK_PATH`/`TEST_MANUAL_FILE_CHECK`) whose fallback path (line 508) invokes:

```
call :runte ClangHLSLTests.dll /p:"HlslDataDir=..." /name:CompilerTest::ManualFileCheckTest
    /runIgnoredTests /p:"InputPath=%MANUAL_FILE_CHECK_PATH%"
```

i.e. one TAEF test (`CompilerTest::ManualFileCheckTest`) that walks whatever single directory
path a developer passes on the command line — not part of `check-all`/CI, and not what the issue
calls a "workflow that works with LIT."

The old GoogleTest/TAEF validator harness, `tools/clang/unittests/HLSL/ValidationTest.cpp`, does
not run these files either:
`git grep -c HLSLFileCheck ... -- tools/clang/unittests/HLSL/ValidationTest.cpp` → 0 matches
(exit 1 / no hits). It is a separate, hand-written C++ test file with its own hardcoded cases; it
does not iterate the `HLSLFileCheck/validation/` tree at all.

**Conclusion for asks 1–3**: still open. No LIT-compatible workflow for DXIL-validator tests
exists at ground truth; the relevant test files are excluded from automatic discovery by design
(`config.suffixes = []`), reachable only via a manual, single-directory TAEF invocation, and the
project continues to add tests to this unreachable tree as recently as Jan 2024.

## Finding 2: a partial LIT migration exists elsewhere, but has no validator subtree

`tools/clang/test/HLSLFileCheckLit/` is a separate, genuinely lit-discovered directory — it
appears in `lit --show-tests` output as `Clang :: HLSLFileCheckLit/...` entries. Its only two
subdirectories are `hlsl` and `passes` (confirmed by directly listing the directory in
`manual-case-lit-validator-coverage.txt`) — there is no `validation` subdirectory. This shows
that a partial LIT migration effort for HLSL codegen/pass tests has begun in the years since this
issue was filed, but it explicitly has not been extended to cover DXIL validator tests, which is
exactly what this issue asks for.

## Finding 3: ask 4 (external validator test coverage) is resolved

The reporter's 2023-02-28 follow-up comment adds: "DXC is also missing test coverage for
external validator workflows." This has since been addressed. `tools/clang/test/DXC/` (a
different, always-lit-discovered directory, unrelated to the `HLSLFileCheck` exclusion above)
now contains:

- `validate_1_6_2112.test`
- `validate_1_7_2308.test`
- `validate_1_8_2502.test`
- `version_interface.test`

These test loading an older/external validator library via `DxcDllExtValidationLoader` and assert
on the resulting version-dependent behaviour — exactly the "external validator workflow" coverage
the comment asked for. Confirmed lit-discovered: all four appear in the
`lit --show-tests build\tools\clang\test\DXC` output in `manual-case-lit-validator-coverage.txt`.

History: `git log --follow -- tools/clang/test/DXC/validate_1_8_2502.test` shows the file's
lineage traces to `e7346acd9d4000035d8383c713ee966a5abdd7cb` (PR #8075, "Fix dxc version printing
and fix external validator testing", 2026-01-22) — itself building on the introduction of
`DxcDllExtValidationLoader` by PR #7749 ("Make DXC and DXV use new DxcDllExtValidationLoader...",
2025-10-27). Both are well before ground truth (2026-08-12) and both are still present/unmodified
by anything after. This specific, narrower ask is resolved.

## Summary

| Ask | Status at ground truth |
|---|---|
| 1–3: LIT-compatible workflow for DXIL validator (`dxv`) tests, replacing `%dxilver` TAEF flow | **Still open** — `HLSLFileCheck/validation/` remains excluded from lit discovery (`config.suffixes = []`, PR #5537, Aug 2023); only reachable via manual `hcttest.cmd -filecheck` invocation of `CompilerTest::ManualFileCheckTest`; new tests are still being added to this unreachable tree as late as Jan 2024 (PR #6172) |
| 4: external validator workflow test coverage | **Resolved** — `tools/clang/test/DXC/validate_1_6_2112.test`, `validate_1_7_2308.test`, `validate_1_8_2502.test`, `version_interface.test` are lit-discovered and cover exactly this, added by PR #7749 (2025-10-27), fixed by PR #8075 (2026-01-22) |

## Caveats / what was not verified

- No attempt was made to actually build or run `check-all`/the LIT suite end-to-end; discovery
  was checked with `lit --show-tests` only (read-only enumeration), per the task's constraint
  against rebuilding/relinking shared targets. This is sufficient to answer "is this test
  reachable by the automated test runner" without needing to execute it.
  `--param=build_mode=Release` was required (not `Debug`) because `llvm-config.exe`, needed by
  `lit.cfg`'s feature detection, is only present under `build\Release\bin` in this environment;
  see `method-notes.md`.
  `--show-tests` against a *build*-tree subdirectory path only resolves correctly when pointed at
  the top-level `build\tools\clang\test` (which loads `lit.site.cfg`); passing a deeper build-tree
  subdirectory path directly (e.g. `build\tools\clang\test\CodeGenHLSL`) reports "contained no
  tests" even for genuinely lit-discovered directories, because file discovery resolves against
  the *source* tree's mirrored path, not a populated build-tree copy. The `HLSLFileCheck`/
  `DXILValidation`/`DXC` commands above were pointed directly at those build-tree leaf paths and
  still resolved correctly/consistently with the source-tree `lit.local.cfg` contents, so this
  caveat does not change the conclusion, but is recorded for the next reader's benefit.
- No PR anywhere references issue #5064 by number (confirmed via the GitHub timeline, zero
  cross-references), so the "still open" / "resolved" determination above rests entirely on
  direct inspection of the current tree and its git history, not on a maintainer's own resolution
  note.
- `.cache/compilers/main-debug.json`'s free-text `provenance_note` field contains stale text
  referencing unrelated older SHAs (a copy-paste/registration artifact from an earlier batch);
  its structured `git_commit` field is correct and is what was relied on here. Not this session's
  artifact to correct (shared cache state, out of the per-issue write boundary).
